whatThisFileIs: A REVIEW RECORD ONLY. It carries no `paths` key, and that omission is deliberate and load-bearing -- see `noPathsOnPurpose` below. It is named AFC-205 because the commit it records (3cb6b0a) is AFC-205's commit; the filename follows the registry convention of being named for the issue whose work the record is about, not for the issue that happened to write the record.

reviews.findings: F1-F6, three blocking (F1 one-hop membership count, F2 membership row does not confer capability, F3 retention_worker NOLOGIN never asserted), all on the deploy-time assertion in bootstrap/0001_roles.sql

noPathsOnPurpose: AFC-238 authorises the reviews[] record for R2 and nothing else. Registering the R1 claim -- the `paths` entry that would say who wrote tests/db/65_retention_worker_membership.sql -- is AFC-221's work and is owned by the CTO. Adding `paths` here would have suppressed the R1 violation `no registered claim covers tests/db/65_retention_worker_membership.sql`, and the acceptance criteria for AFC-238 require that violation to still be reported. The R1 claim and the R2 review record are deliberately left on opposite sides of that line. There is no mechanism in this registry that ties them together, and there is no way for one agent to hold both without one of them being wrong: `claimed_by()` reads only `paths`, `review_record()` reads only `reviews`, so the two are independent by construction.
authorAgentIdOmittedOnPurpose: A claim's authorAgentId is an attribution of authorship, and authorship of 3cb6b0a is not mine to record. git already holds it: `git log -1 3cb6b0a` shows MediaTech (CTO, 8f6e42d7-fb6e-4e6c-904b-dfdda50000ed) as the committer of both roles and the suite. Transcribing it here would put the CTO's authorship claim in a file written by their reviewer, which is the shape that lets a registry start approving itself. The CTO registers it with the paths in AFC-221.
reviewerIsNotAuthor: This entry is written by the reviewer, and the reviewer's agent id is the one recorded. The reviewer does not report to the author. Per AFC-194 section 5 a CTO-authored compliance-path commit would nominally take 'Reviewed-by: Operations', and the CEO ruled that is a disclosure rather than a review and will not be counted as a second signature -- so the author cannot transcribe this verdict and have it count. The verdict was reached by independent review, proved by execution against pristine fixtures, and re-verified at a later HEAD because the tree had moved. Source issue: AFC-215, six findings, three blocking. That issue is the evidence; this file is only the index entry pointing at it.
trailerPresentOnCommitIsFalse: Verified against the commit, not assumed. `git log -1 --format=%B 3cb6b0a` contains the line `Reviewed by: MediaTech (CTO, decision and implementation) and SecurityEngineer (independent security review, scheduled).` -- note the space in `Reviewed by:`. The guard extracts a trailer with `sed -n 's/^Reviewed-by:[[:space:]]*//p'`, which requires the hyphen, so this line is not a trailer in the sense the guard recognises and R2 correctly reported the commit as unreviewed. It also names two reviewers jointly, which is a second reason it could not serve as a form-1 record even if the spelling matched: the reviewer of record is one agent, named in the entry above.
correctionToTheAFC238Brief: The AFC-238 description names two R2 paths for this commit: tests/db/65_retention_worker_membership.sql and scripts/run-db-tests.mjs. The second is wrong. REVIEW_REQUIRED_PATHS in scripts/dirty-path-guard.sh is exactly four globs -- services/directus/schema/engine/**, services/directus/schema/migrations/**, tests/db/**, and scripts/retention-literal-gate.sh -- and scripts/run-db-tests.mjs matches none of them. The guard's own baseline confirms it: run against HEAD it reports for 3cb6b0a a single flagged path, tests/db/65_retention_worker_membership.sql. scripts/run-db-tests.mjs is on the DIRTY-guard list (all of scripts/) and not on the R2 list; conflating the two lists is the specific defect self-test assertion 9e exists to catch, so the correction is recorded rather than repeated. This does not change the remedy: one reviews[] entry covers the commit regardless of how many of its paths are on the list.
doesNotClaim: A claim asserts authorship, not correctness. This file asserts neither: it carries a review record and no paths. It is not a licence, it exempts nothing from scripts/retention-literal-gate.sh, and it does not make 3cb6b0a a good commit -- only reviewed, which is a different and much smaller claim. The verdict recorded above is ADVERSE in three places, and a review record naming an adverse verdict closes the R2 provenance requirement without closing a single one of the three blocking findings.
stillOpenAfterThisRecord: R1 on 3cb6b0a: two violations remain and this file suppresses neither -- no registered claim covers tests/db/65_retention_worker_membership.sql, and the commit carries no Issue: trailer (the message ends with the prose line 'AFC-205.', which is not the trailer the guard reads). Both belong to AFC-221, owned by the CTO. AFC-205 itself remains open with F1-F3 unfixed in the committed tree as of this record; the fixes are the author's.
notClearanceOfThe0105Gate: AFC-215 supplied evidence to the CEO for the section 0.10.5 retention evidence gate and explicitly did not clear it. This file is a provenance record of that review. It is not clearance of that gate, and no reader should treat an R2 line reading 'ok R2 review record' as evidence that the retention control is sound. The gate is the CEO's to clear.
